name: Lombard Street to Coit Tower (OSM network bake)

provenance.author: tools/gis

sources.name: USGS 3DEP elevation
sources.attribution: Map services and data available from U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program.
sources.query: https://elevation.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/3DEPElevation/ImageServer/getSamples getSamples multipoint, 192 points in 1 request(s) (lon, lat WGS84, sha256 fc3f08ef46633f8d), bilinear (line lombard)

provenance.modifications: 1 real Lombard Street and Telegraph Hill Boulevard paths stitched through the OSM graph, heading Gaussian-smoothed, positions re-integrated from heading, then pinned back onto the real junctions (largest drift closed 0.0 m, spread back along each line), resampled at 2 m with curvature from the sampled positions; land elevation from 3DEP low-pass filtered, bridge decks synthesized (3DEP is bare earth); lanes simplified to the configured cross-section; junction connector roads synthesized (a turn, a straight and a turn)

meta.notes: A real-road network (playtest 3, T9.3; the maintainer, 2026-10-03: "hairpin races like Lombard", "real road layouts"): Lombard Street east from Polk Street, up to the crest at Hyde Street, down the crooked block (the real eight hairpins, one-way and one lane wide, red brick), on along Lombard to Telegraph Hill Boulevard and up to the circle at Coit Tower. The smoothing is 2 m, tight enough to keep the hairpins (a wider one rounds them away); the crooked block is sampled every metre so its 5 m turns keep their shape, and a lane is the whole road there, since a two-way table fails the road format's width rule on a 5 m radius (a 1.5 m planter verge each side stands beyond it). Cross streets are pass-through only.
